status: M1.8-N4B5R runtime candidate; not yet human-accepted
rule: The accepted M1.8-N4B1C lateral dual-path decoder, unchanged, under the M1.8-N4B5R elevation-aware paddle tilt geometry. Only the Retina input changes, and only while the paddle is tilted (face < 1) and seen at high elevation.

escape_decoder.spike_inference_rule: per side: spike_t = trace_t - decay * trace_{t-1} >= 0.5, with decay = float32(exp(-tick_seconds / trace_tau_seconds)); no spike is inferred on the first sample after reset
escape_decoder.lateral_rule: left and right tracked independently; the qualifying spike must be on the current sample; the previous spike of the SAME side must be at most lateral_window_samples samples earlier; a left spike followed by a right spike never qualifies
escape_decoder.window_rule: one summed qualification flag per sample, refractory samples included; cleared when an escape fires and on reset
reset_clears: lateral spike history and previous trace values
escape_decoder.motor_semantics: unchanged: strength, side, steering, saccade, forward bias and refractory do not depend on the path that fired

sustained_threshold.basis: inherited unchanged from the scalar single-sample calibration, used here only as the summed qualification level

summed_path.basis: the M1.8-N2b summed criterion, unchanged; N2b itself failed its second human re-acceptance and is retained here only as the path that keeps alternating-side hover evidence

lateral_path.basis: M1.8-N4A: spontaneous DNp01 spikes are noise driven and independent per side, and the summed trace turns bilateral coincidences into apparent multi-spike evidence; M1.8-N4B1: a same-side 60 ms rule (frozen Rule A) restores legacy-level committed-strike timing with 0 false events on a fresh 280-minute N0; M1.8-N4B1C: combined with the N2b path it restores alternating-side hover coverage and passes a new pre-registered 280-minute N0 holdout. The window is a simulator property (LIF reset to 0 plus independent noise), not a biological refractory constant.

geometry.formula: half = paddle_radius * (e + (1 - e) * face) * (1 - tilt_anisotropy * cos(elevation) * (1 - face) * abs(sin(bearing - orientation))), with cos(elevation) = horizontal fly-paddle distance / 3-D fly-paddle distance
geometry.previous_formula: half = paddle_radius * (e + (1 - e) * face) * (1 - tilt_anisotropy * (1 - face) * abs(sin(bearing - orientation)))
geometry.scope: ROOM configuration only; GAME and LAB configurations are unchanged
geometry.reason: correction of the overhead tilt-foreshortening artifact: the bearing-only term turns horizontal bearing rate into apparent expansion of up to 6.9 rad/s under a stationary paddle (0.13 rad/s from range change), producing all overhead free-flight escapes of M1.8-N4B4 and the episode-5 slow-close signal
geometry.parameter_class: C (geometric rendering correction, not a biological parameter)

hash_convention: decoder_record and research files: SHA256 of committed content with CRLF normalised to LF; config_sha256: raw working-file bytes

decoder_record.note: the accepted N4B1C decoder record; it continues to match the accepted N4B1C ROOM configuration (commit e3c55b3)

measurement_conditions.note: fly position and heading are fixed; velocity stays zero, wander is disabled, and collisions/escape actions are disabled

measurement_reuse.kind: geometry runtime candidate; decoder transferred unchanged; not a new measurement
measurement_reuse.reason: The decoder parameters are not re-derived. The fixed-fly no-loom measurements behind them see a settled, static paddle, whose encoder drive is zero under either geometry; the geometry changes only the time course of the apparent size of a tilted paddle seen at high elevation. Runtime validation of the candidate is produced by tools/n4b5r_runtime_validation.py.
